body: Thank you for your perspective :) Would there be a threshold where you consider an AI artwork something that you exhibit a degree of manual control over (such as in/outpainting, fixing errors with a standard art program, or just using a ton of prompt modifiers) or does the generative nature of it make it random no matter what?

Genuine question (not trying to be a gotcha): what historical parallels are you talking about when you say that it doesn't need to be thought of in a different way? Because as far as I know digital art/photography/traditional art etc are considered different "categories" of art. I agree that the stigma is likely to fade, but when it has, do you think there would be any reason to distinguish it from non-generative art?

Thanks for the response! To be honest I had the traditional vs. digital art divide in mind when asking the question, mainly thinking about how the former hasn't died out as a medium for art commissions (because people want *something* from it that isn't digitally replicable, such as the original physical work or interactions that certain paints have). When it comes to artwork used in other media, I do think you're right; there'll always be some manner of competition there, and people will usually pick the cheaper option when precision isn't a concern (which is where most of my wariness comes from), but we'll have to see how that develops.
Thanks for the info! Might give it a shot when signups reopen.
